access_denial_tests.name: principal-controller must not see cr-policy-delivery

access_denial_tests.name: principal-hr-policy-owner must not see gap-policy-delivery-receipts

access_denial_tests.name: principal-controller must not see kf-close-fx-time

The controller reads knowledge_fragments but is not granted the stewardship diagnostic columns. evidence_has_expired EXISTS on public.vw_knowledge_fragments and must be ABSENT from the controller's view -- selecting it must raise 'column does not exist', not return null.

access_denial_tests.name: principal-close-automation must not see

app_role_profiles.name: Chief Financial Officer (human)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Decide whether the attestation can be signed, and what the green actually rests on.

app_role_profiles.name: Corporate Controller (human)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Prove the close controls worked — not merely that nothing failed.

app_role_profiles.name: Finance Analyst (human)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Check my own steps before somebody else does.

app_role_profiles.name: People Policy Owner (human)
app_role_profiles.pitch: See what is live in my name and what is waiting on me.

app_role_profiles.name: Employment Counsel (human)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Hold the four legal gates: consent, quiet hours, review, retention.

app_role_profiles.name: Employee Communications Manager (human)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Follow a message from my approval to whether anyone actually got it.

app_role_profiles.name: Procedural Knowledge Steward (human)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Keep procedural knowledge current, owned, and exercised.

app_role_profiles.name: Procedural Knowledge Authority (human)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Approve semantic change, and know what the model's claims rest on.

app_role_profiles.name: Close Automation Operator (software)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Confirm I am authorized and my inputs are fresh before I run.

app_role_profiles.name: Variance Review Agent (software)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Check my authority, my boundary, and my quality against the human baseline.

app_role_profiles.name: Policy Drafting Agent (software)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Confirm my sources are approved and I have not created a commitment.

app_role_profiles.name: Notification Publisher (software)
app_role_profiles.pitch: Clear four gates before transmitting, and leave a record of every refusal.

app_routes.name: Can I Sign? — /cfo/attestation
app_routes.purpose: The one screen I open first. A single verdict for the close I am being asked to attest to, and if the answer is no, the named blocker.
app_routes.layout_hints: Hero verdict card (green/red) with the IsAttestationReady column and, beneath it, a blocker list. Right rail: assurance grade summary. Nothing below the fold that is not a blocker.

app_routes.name: Blockers — /cfo/attestation/blockers
app_routes.purpose: Every reason I cannot sign yet, each one traced to the row that produced it.
app_routes.layout_hints: Ordered list, most severe first. Each row: the blocking condition, the entity it fires on, and a link into that entity's detail route. Empty state must say 'no blockers' explicitly, never render blank.

app_routes.name: Assurance Grade — /cfo/assurance/grade
app_routes.purpose: When the verdict reads TRUE, what proportion of the controls behind that TRUE were actually demonstrated to work — versus asserted by an interested party, versus never exercised at all.
app_routes.layout_hints: Three-band stacked bar: demonstrated / asserted / never-exercised. Below it, the per-control table that produced the bands. The headline number is the grade, not the verdict.

app_routes.name: Controls Nobody Watches — /cfo/assurance/unwitnessed
app_routes.purpose: The requirements I am personally attesting to that have no computed witness — and the named human who would answer for each if it failed.
app_routes.layout_hints: Table: requirement, blocking?, has-witness?, accountable human, their role. Rows with no witness AND blocking are the emphasis. Each row links to the requirement detail.

app_routes.name: Typed, Not Computed — /cfo/assurance/typed-conclusions
app_routes.purpose: Every control claim in this model that rests on a human typing a conclusion rather than on something computed.
app_routes.layout_hints: Two-column split: computed claims vs typed claims, with counts. The typed side is the working list. Each entry shows who typed it and when.

app_routes.name: Who Witnessed the Witnesses — /cfo/assurance/independence
app_routes.purpose: Across the whole close, is there any independent human observation at all — or is every layer the same handful of people confirming each other?
app_routes.layout_hints: Chain/graph view: approvals and verification outcomes as nodes, edges where one person confirms another. Self-witnessed loops highlighted. Sidebar counts independent vs self-witnessed.

app_routes.name: Who Held Authority — /cfo/authority/accountability
app_routes.purpose: For every approval in this close, the human who was personally accountable — and whether an exception routed authority away from the person who normally holds it.
app_routes.layout_hints: Table per approval: approver, role held at the time, normal holder, exception invoked?. Rerouted rows flagged. Links to the exception invocation detail.

app_routes.name: My Own Approvals — /cfo/authority/my-approvals
app_routes.purpose: My approval on se-close06 — is there anything behind it other than the fact that I clicked approve?
app_routes.layout_hints: Detail card per approval I gave: what was verified, by whom, with what evidence. An approval with nothing behind it is rendered as a warning state, not an empty section.

app_routes.name: What My Signature Rests On — /cfo/attestation/dependencies
app_routes.purpose: The full set of controls, versions, and evidence records my signature actually depends on — the blast radius of my own name.
app_routes.layout_hints: Dependency tree rooted at the attestation, expanding into controls, versions, evidence. Each node shows its current state. This is the reference view the change-watch route diffs against.

app_routes.name: Changed Since I Signed — /cfo/attestation/changed-since
app_routes.purpose: Since the moment I signed, has anything changed that would have altered my decision — specifically touching a control, a version, or an evidence record my signature depended on.
app_routes.layout_hints: Timeline diff anchored at the signature timestamp. Only changes intersecting the dependency set are shown; unrelated churn is explicitly excluded and the exclusion is stated.

app_routes.name: Would It Survive Restatement — /cfo/assurance/restatement
app_routes.purpose: If I re-run every attestation column against this same data six months from now, will it give the same answer? Name every column whose value depends on when it is read.
app_routes.layout_hints: Table of attestation columns with a tense-dependent flag, sourced from the EvaluationContexts modelled instant. Time-dependent columns get an explicit warning band at the top.

app_routes.name: Attestation Detail — /cfo/attestation/execution/:executionId
app_routes.purpose: One execution, everything I would be signing for it.
app_routes.layout_hints: Full-page record: execution header, per-step conformance, control results, evidence links. Reachable from the blocker list and the home verdict.

app_routes.name: Control Board — /controller/controls
app_routes.purpose: Every close control at a glance: which fired, which held, and which are structurally incapable of failing.
app_routes.layout_hints: Grid of control tiles, each showing bound steps, witness presence, and whether it has ever produced a negative. Inoperative controls are visually distinct, not just sorted lower.

app_routes.name: Inoperative Controls — /controller/controls/inoperative
app_routes.purpose: Which of my blocking close controls are structurally incapable of failing — declared, bound to a step, and yet with no mechanism that could ever produce a negative result.
app_routes.layout_hints: List with a three-state badge per control: has-witness / witness-ever-fired / could-ever-fire. The third state is the finding. Each row explains WHY it cannot fire.

app_routes.name: Witness Scope vs Binding — /controller/controls/witness-scope
app_routes.purpose: For each control with a witness, is the witness evaluated at the same steps where the control is bound? req-close-evidence is bound to close-03 and close-08 — is its witness scoped to both?
app_routes.layout_hints: Two parallel columns per control: steps bound vs steps witnessed, with the set difference called out. A non-empty difference is the finding.

app_routes.name: Separation of Duties — /controller/controls/separation-of-duties
app_routes.purpose: Did the same agent both prepare and approve any part of this close — computed, not asserted. And could it even have happened, or is the control passing because the structure never gave it the chance to fail?
app_routes.layout_hints: Top: the computed verdict. Below: the opportunity analysis — executions where the same agent COULD have held both seats. A pass with zero opportunity is rendered as inconclusive, not green.

app_routes.name: Spec vs Execution — /controller/execution/conformance
app_routes.purpose: One number per close: did the execution actually conform to its procedure version, and if not, how far off was it?
app_routes.layout_hints: Reuse the existing spec/execution ledger layout. Add a single conformance score in the header. Divergent steps anchor-linked from the score.

app_routes.name: Divergence Nobody Governed — /controller/execution/ungoverned-divergence
app_routes.purpose: For each divergence, was there a governing instrument behind it — an invoked exception, an approved change request, a recorded deviation with an owner — or did the run simply do something different and nobody wrote it down?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per divergence: the instrument that covers it, or an explicit 'ungoverned' state. Ungoverned rows are the working list and sort first.

app_routes.name: Authority at Time of Approval — /controller/authority/validity
app_routes.purpose: Every approval on this close — was it given by an agent who actually held the required role AT THE TIME they approved, not just someone who holds it today?
app_routes.layout_hints: Timeline per approval: the assignment window vs the approval instant. Approvals outside their window are the finding. Bitemporal — do not compare against today.

app_routes.name: Machine Did Human Work — /controller/authority/ai-boundary
app_routes.purpose: Did any AI agent or automated pipeline execute a step that requires human confirmation, or sign off on something a human was supposed to own?
app_routes.layout_hints: Table of software-executed steps against their human-confirmation requirement. Include an explicit 'never approached' column — an untested boundary is not a passing one.

app_routes.name: Asserted, Not Demonstrated — /controller/evidence/asserted
app_routes.purpose: Three satisfaction records are asserted-only. For each: who asserted it, did they have any independent basis, and were they the same person who executed the step they were scoring?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per record: asserter, executor, independence verdict. Same-person rows flagged. Evidence URI shown or its absence stated explicitly.

app_routes.name: Control Detail — /controller/controls/requirement/:requirementId
app_routes.purpose: One control, end to end: what it says, where it is bound, what witnesses it, and every time it has been evaluated.
app_routes.layout_hints: Detail page. Header with the statement and blocking flag; sections for bindings, witness, and evaluation history. This is the shared requirement detail specialised for the controller.

app_routes.name: My Steps — /finance-analyst/my-work
app_routes.purpose: The steps I personally executed, and whether each one closed cleanly or closed past something.
app_routes.layout_hints: Card per step execution with status, duration vs expected, and blocking-control state. Anything that closed past a blocking control is the emphasis.

app_routes.name: Closed Past a Control — /finance-analyst/my-work/blocking-unmet
app_routes.purpose: On the steps I personally executed, did any close out while a BLOCKING requirement was still not fully satisfied?
app_routes.layout_hints: List of my step executions with an unmet blocking control, each showing the control and its satisfaction level. This is a personal-exposure screen — keep it short and unambiguous.

app_routes.name: Never Assessed — /finance-analyst/my-work/never-evaluated
app_routes.purpose: Which blocking requirements were attached to a step I ran but never got a satisfaction record at all — not satisfied, not unsatisfied, just never assessed.
app_routes.layout_hints: The absence IS the finding, so render missing records as explicit rows, never as an empty table.

app_routes.name: Late and Unexplained — /finance-analyst/my-work/late-unexplained
app_routes.purpose: Which of my steps ran long without anybody recording why — and of those, which had an exception available that nobody invoked.
app_routes.layout_hints: Table: step, actual vs expected, deviation recorded?, exception available?, exception invoked?. The available-but-not-invoked combination is the finding.

app_routes.name: Declared vs Performed — /finance-analyst/evidence/verification-performed
app_routes.purpose: For every step I ran that had a declared verification, did anybody actually perform it and record the observed signal — or did I just get a PASS with nothing behind it?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per step: declared verification, observed signal or its absence, who observed. A PASS with no observation is rendered as hollow, not green.

app_routes.name: My Own Evidence Quality — /finance-analyst/evidence/my-evidence
app_routes.purpose: On the steps I ran, was the person who observed the passing signal ever me — and when it was, did I at least attach an evidence URI?
app_routes.layout_hints: Self-witness table scoped to my steps: observer, is-me flag, evidence URI present. Self-witnessed with no URI is the weakest state and should read that way.

app_routes.name: Was My Source Fresh — /finance-analyst/evidence/source-freshness
app_routes.purpose: When I attested my reconciliation, was the underlying ledger data actually fresh — or was I certifying against a source that had already gone stale under its own SLA?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per binding: freshness SLA, age at run, authoritative flag. Judged against the modelled instant, never the wall clock.

app_routes.name: Stale Then vs Stale Now — /finance-analyst/evidence/stale-then-vs-now
app_routes.purpose: Was the source stale AT THE MOMENT I RAN, or has it merely gone stale since — and are those the same steps?
app_routes.layout_hints: Two-column comparison: staleness at run-time vs staleness at the current evaluation context. The delta between the columns is the whole point of the screen.

app_routes.name: Clean, or Just Unchecked — /finance-analyst/quality/clean-but-uncovered
app_routes.purpose: Of the executions that ARE clean, how many are clean because everything was checked and passed, versus clean because there was almost nothing checking them?
app_routes.layout_hints: Scatter or two-axis table: controls-checked against controls-passed. Low-check/high-pass is the quadrant of interest and should be labelled as such.

app_routes.name: Cleared by a Mute Control — /finance-analyst/quality/cleared-by-mute-control
app_routes.purpose: How many of the blocking controls that cleared me have NEVER produced a negative outcome anywhere in this model — and were any of my steps cleared ONLY by controls of that kind?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per step: clearing controls, each tagged with whether it has ever fired negative. A step cleared exclusively by never-fired controls is the headline finding.

app_routes.name: Coverage of My Controls — /finance-analyst/quality/witness-coverage
app_routes.purpose: Of the blocking controls attached to the steps I run, how many have no computed witness — and is HasComputedWitness even telling me the truth, given a human typed it in by hand?
app_routes.layout_hints: Coverage bar plus a caveat band: the declared-vs-actual witness comparison, because the declaration itself is a typed field and must be shown as such.

app_routes.name: What I Own — /hr-policy-owner/ownership
app_routes.purpose: Everything currently live under my name: policy versions, knowledge claims, and the decisions waiting on me.
app_routes.layout_hints: Three-panel dashboard: owned versions, owned claims (with approval state), pending decisions with age. Unapproved-but-live claims are the emphasis.

app_routes.name: Unapproved in My Name — /hr-policy-owner/ownership/unapproved
app_routes.purpose: Which claims am I the owner of that were never approved — and are any of them routing real cases right now?
app_routes.layout_hints: List of owned fragments by status, with an 'operationally live' flag. Reviewed-but-not-Approved AND live is the finding.

app_routes.name: Blast Radius of a Claim — /hr-policy-owner/ownership/blast-radius/:fragmentId
app_routes.purpose: How many steps, exceptions and authority boundaries currently depend on a claim I have not signed, and how long has it been sitting at Reviewed?
app_routes.layout_hints: Dependency fan-out from one fragment: steps, exceptions, boundaries. Header carries the age at Reviewed. This is the screen that makes an unsigned claim feel expensive.

app_routes.name: Waiting On Me — /hr-policy-owner/backlog
app_routes.purpose: What decisions are waiting on me personally, and how long have they been waiting.
app_routes.layout_hints: Queue ordered by age. Each item shows what it blocks downstream, so the cost of my delay is visible from the queue itself.

app_routes.name: What My Delay Blocks — /hr-policy-owner/backlog/downstream
app_routes.purpose: The full chain from my inbox outward: which knowledge gaps stay open because I have not decided, which steps sit downstream, and how many days of that delay are mine personally.
app_routes.layout_hints: Chain view: my pending decision → blocked gap → downstream steps. Attribute delay days to me vs to the process explicitly; do not conflate them.

app_routes.name: What I Have Cleared — /hr-policy-owner/backlog/my-decisions
app_routes.purpose: How many decisions have I made that the model still displays as outstanding against me? I cannot show what I have actually cleared.
app_routes.layout_hints: Decision history with the terminal-state problem surfaced: Approved requests still counted open are flagged as a model defect, not hidden.

app_routes.name: Is the AI Boundary Held — /hr-policy-owner/governance/ai-boundary
app_routes.purpose: kf-policy-ai-boundary says AI may draft but may not create legal commitments. Is that boundary actually being held?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per boundary: assigned agent, executions, and whether a violation was possible. Pair every 'no violation' with an 'ever approached' count — the two together are the real answer.

app_routes.name: Knowledge Half-Life — /hr-policy-owner/governance/knowledge-half-life
app_routes.purpose: Is the policy I own now resting on knowledge older than the policy itself has been reviewed?
app_routes.layout_hints: Timeline: elicitation dates, version issue date, review cadence, next due. The comparison between knowledge age and review interval is the headline.

app_routes.name: What Departed With Them — /hr-policy-owner/governance/departed-holders
app_routes.purpose: Somebody's assignment ended. Did anything they owned or sourced go with them — claims, gaps, pending decisions — or did the departure genuinely leave nothing behind?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per departed assignment: everything sourced or owned by that agent, with current ownership state. Orphaned items are the finding.

app_routes.name: What Was Actually Sent — /hr-policy-owner/delivery/what-was-sent
app_routes.purpose: If an employee disputes what they received, can I show that what was sent matched what I approved?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per delivery: approved text vs transmitted text, side by side, with the approval record and date. A mismatch is the finding; identical is stated explicitly.

app_routes.name: Compliance Gates — /employment-counsel/compliance
app_routes.purpose: The four gates I care about — consent, quiet hours, legal review, retention — each as a pass/fail with the breaching rows named.
app_routes.layout_hints: Four gate tiles across the top; a breach list beneath whichever is selected. A gate with zero breaches must distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'never evaluated'.

app_routes.name: SMS Without Consent — /employment-counsel/compliance/consent
app_routes.purpose: Did we send an SMS to any recipient who had not given SMS consent at the moment we sent it?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per SMS delivery: recipient, consent state at send time, verdict. Bitemporal — consent today is not the question.

app_routes.name: Quiet Hours — /employment-counsel/compliance/quiet-hours
app_routes.purpose: Did any SMS go out between 20:00 and 08:00 in the recipient's own local time?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per delivery: send instant, recipient timezone, local hour, verdict. Show the local-time conversion explicitly — the timezone is the whole difficulty.

app_routes.name: Sent Before My Review — /employment-counsel/compliance/legal-review
app_routes.purpose: Did any message go out before my legal review of the underlying policy version was actually complete?
app_routes.layout_hints: Timeline per campaign: review completion vs first transmission. Sends preceding review completion are the finding.

app_routes.name: Retention Evidence — /employment-counsel/compliance/retention
app_routes.purpose: Do we still hold the exact text of every message we sent, for the full 2555-day retention period the policy commits us to?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per delivery: text retained?, retention deadline, days remaining. Missing text is a breach and must render as one.

app_routes.name: Unreachable, Not Acknowledged — /employment-counsel/compliance/unreachable
app_routes.purpose: For every recipient we could not reach, did we correctly refrain from marking their acknowledgement complete?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per unreachable recipient: delivery state, acknowledgement state. An acknowledgement on an unreachable recipient is the finding.

app_routes.name: Campaign Board — /communications-manager/delivery
app_routes.purpose: For this policy run: who we meant to reach, who we actually reached, and where the rest went.
app_routes.layout_hints: Funnel across the top (intended → sent → delivered → acknowledged), with each drop-off clickable into the rows that fell out.

app_routes.name: Approval-to-Delivery Yield — /communications-manager/delivery/yield
app_routes.purpose: Of everybody the pipeline intended to contact, what fraction actually received it — and where exactly did the rest go?
app_routes.layout_hints: Sankey or stepped funnel with an explicit terminal bucket for every loss: refused, bounced, suppressed, deferred. No row may vanish without a bucket.

app_routes.name: Bounced and Unworked — /communications-manager/delivery/failed
app_routes.purpose: How many recipients are sitting in a bounced or failed state that nobody is working?
app_routes.layout_hints: Worklist, not a report: each failed delivery with age and owner. Unowned failures sort first.

app_routes.name: Approved Before Sending — /communications-manager/governance/approval-authority
app_routes.purpose: Was every template we actually sent approved by me — the ApprovalRole the policy names — before it went out?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per sent template: approval record, approver role, approval instant vs send instant. Sends preceding approval are the finding.

app_routes.name: Edited After I Approved — /communications-manager/governance/template-drift
app_routes.purpose: Has any template been edited since I approved it, and did we send the edited version under cover of my old approval?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per template: approval timestamp, last edit timestamp, sends after the edit. Edit-then-send-on-old-approval is the finding.

app_routes.name: Freeze What I Approved — /communications-manager/governance/frozen-approval/:deliveryId
app_routes.purpose: For a message we sent last month, can I still show what I approved — the exact text, the exact approval, on the exact date — without that answer changing the next time somebody edits the template?
app_routes.layout_hints: Immutable snapshot view: the text as sent, the approval as given. Must read from the frozen delivery record, never from the live template.

app_routes.name: Opt-Out Text — /communications-manager/compliance/optout
app_routes.purpose: Did every SMS we actually transmitted carry the approved opt-out text?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per SMS: transmitted text, opt-out present?. Missing opt-out is a breach row.

app_routes.name: Oversized SMS — /communications-manager/compliance/sms-limits
app_routes.purpose: Did any SMS we sent exceed 160 characters or split into more than 3 segments?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per SMS: character count, segment count, both against their limits. Show the computed integer, not a re-derived length.

app_routes.name: Why Nobody Answered — /communications-manager/audience/engagement
app_routes.purpose: One acknowledgement out of six deliveries. Is that because employees ignored us, or because the messages that landed were the least likely to be answered — wrong channel, wrong template, sent into the small hours?
app_routes.layout_hints: Cross-tab of acknowledgement rate by channel, template, and send hour. The point is to separate audience apathy from our own targeting.

app_routes.name: Correctly Refused, Then Forgotten — /communications-manager/audience/suppression
app_routes.purpose: When we correctly refused to reach somebody, did anyone ever go back and reach them another way — or does 'correctly refused' quietly mean 'never communicated with again'?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per suppressed recipient: the refusal reason, and any subsequent successful contact on another channel. No follow-up is the finding.

app_routes.name: Refused, or Overridden — /communications-manager/governance/authorization-override
app_routes.purpose: When the pipeline refused to send, was it refusing on a rule I set — or overriding an authorization I had already given, for a reason nobody routed back to me?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per refusal: the governing rule, its owner, and whether it contradicts a standing authorization of mine. Contradictions are the finding.

app_routes.name: Pre-Flight — /close-automation/readiness
app_routes.purpose: Before I execute anything: am I authorized, are my inputs fresh, and did my last run leave a mess.
app_routes.layout_hints: Four go/no-go tiles (authority, inputs, prior run, controls) resolving to a single may-I-run verdict. Built for a supervisor watching the agent as much as for the agent.

app_routes.name: Am I Authorized — /close-automation/readiness/authority
app_routes.purpose: Is my own role assignment currently valid, and is the agent named in that assignment actually me?
app_routes.layout_hints: Assignment card: validity window, named agent, identity match. An identity mismatch must halt, not warn.

app_routes.name: Are My Inputs Fresh — /close-automation/readiness/input-freshness
app_routes.purpose: Before I extract: is every operational binding this step reads inside its freshness SLA, and is it the authoritative one?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per binding: age, SLA, authoritative flag. Two independent failure modes — stale, and non-authoritative — must not be collapsed into one badge.

app_routes.name: Controls Scored — /close-automation/readiness/blocking-controls
app_routes.purpose: For each step I am about to run, has every blocking requirement actually been evaluated — or am I about to execute past a control that nobody scored?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per upcoming step: blocking controls and their evaluation state. Unscored controls block the run.

app_routes.name: Last Run Clean — /close-automation/readiness/last-run
app_routes.purpose: Did my previous run leave anything unresolved — an open issue, a WARN, or a deviation — that I should refuse to run on top of?
app_routes.layout_hints: Prior-run summary with an explicit refuse-to-proceed state. Unresolved items are listed individually, never summarised to a count alone.

app_routes.name: Am I Drifting — /close-automation/self-check/override-drift
app_routes.purpose: Are humans overriding or correcting my output more often now than they used to?
app_routes.layout_hints: Override rate over time with the baseline period marked. Call out sample size — a trend on three decisions is not a trend.

app_routes.name: Am I Fit to Decide — /variance-review-agent/self-check
app_routes.purpose: My authority, my boundary, and the currency of the knowledge I triage against — as one verdict.
app_routes.layout_hints: Three-part readiness card: authority provenance, boundary validity, knowledge currency. Any expired component invalidates the whole.

app_routes.name: By What Authority — /variance-review-agent/self-check/authority
app_routes.purpose: By what authority am I executing close-04, when did that authority begin, who approved it, and who held this role before me?
app_routes.layout_hints: Provenance chain: assignment, approver, start instant, predecessor. The handover is part of the answer, not a footnote.

app_routes.name: Who Decided a Machine Should Hold This — /variance-review-agent/self-check/handover
app_routes.route_name: Who Decided a Machine Should Hold This
app_routes.purpose: Mine is the one non-human assignment with a recorded approving authority. Who decided a machine should hold this role, and on what basis?
app_routes.layout_hints: The approving decision as a first-class record: who, when, rationale. If the basis is absent, say so — do not present the approval alone as sufficient.

app_routes.name: Inside My Boundary — /variance-review-agent/governance/boundary
app_routes.purpose: Am I operating inside my approved boundary — or have I made a decision that kf-policy-ai-boundary says only a human may make?
app_routes.layout_hints: Boundary statement, decisions evaluated against it, verdict per decision. Pair with the 'ever tested' count from the ratification route.

app_routes.name: My Boundary's Own Validity — /variance-review-agent/governance/boundary-ratification
app_routes.purpose: The boundary that constrains what I am allowed to decide is ratified by a knowledge fragment that is not current. Is the rule governing me still valid?
app_routes.layout_hints: Fragment validity chain behind the boundary. An expired ratifier makes the boundary itself questionable, and the page must say that plainly.

app_routes.name: Did a Human Confirm — /variance-review-agent/governance/human-confirmation
app_routes.purpose: close-04's instruction says 'Use AI triage, then apply human judgment.' Did a human actually confirm my materiality calls, or did my output pass through unchallenged?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per decision: human confirmation present?, who, when. Unconfirmed decisions on a human-confirmation step are the finding.

app_routes.name: Is My Knowledge Current — /variance-review-agent/knowledge/currency
app_routes.purpose: Is the judgment knowledge I triage against still valid, still owned by someone, and has it been reviewed since it was written?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per fragment: validity, owner, last review. An unowned or unreviewed fragment degrades every decision made against it.

app_routes.name: Better or Worse Than the Human — /variance-review-agent/quality/vs-human-baseline
app_routes.route_name: Better or Worse Than the Human
app_routes.purpose: Since I took over, is my triage quality better or worse than maria-chen's during the prior period?
app_routes.layout_hints: Side-by-side period comparison. Sample size shown at equal prominence to the delta — this is the screen most likely to be over-read.

app_routes.name: Is My Comparison Empty — /variance-review-agent/quality/sample-size
app_routes.purpose: QualityRegressedVsPredecessor says I have not regressed — on the strength of three decisions. Is my comparison statistically empty?
app_routes.layout_hints: Explicit power/sample-size statement. A verdict computed on too few observations must be rendered as inconclusive, not as a pass.

app_routes.name: Correction or Judgment — /variance-review-agent/quality/override-signal
app_routes.purpose: One of my three decisions was overridden. Was that a correction of an error I made, or a human exercising judgment I was never authorized to exercise?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per override: my decision, the human's decision, the stated reason, and which of the two categories it falls in. Uncategorised overrides are themselves a gap.

app_routes.name: What Would Make Me Stop — /variance-review-agent/self-check/stop-condition
app_routes.purpose: Every witness in this model detects something after it has happened. Is there any condition, computed and named, that would stop me before I act?
app_routes.layout_hints: Inventory of stop conditions: pre-act vs post-hoc. If none are pre-act, the page must state that as the finding rather than listing post-hoc witnesses as if they qualified.

app_routes.name: May I Draft — /policy-drafting-agent/readiness
app_routes.purpose: Before I draft: approved sources, valid bindings, and a role assignment that actually exists.
app_routes.layout_hints: Go/no-go card combining source approval, binding freshness, and assignment presence. A missing assignment is a hard stop.

app_routes.name: Approved Sources — /policy-drafting-agent/readiness/sources
app_routes.purpose: Is every resource I am about to read an approved source, and is its binding still inside its freshness window?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per source: approval state, binding age, SLA. Unapproved or stale sources block the draft.

app_routes.name: Do I Have an Assignment — /policy-drafting-agent/readiness/my-assignment
app_routes.purpose: I am named as CurrentAgent and I executed se-policy03 — but is there any RoleAssignment actually granting me that authority?
app_routes.layout_hints: The absence is the finding. If no assignment exists, render that as a violation state, never as an empty list.

app_routes.name: Did I Create a Commitment — /policy-drafting-agent/governance/commitment-boundary
app_routes.purpose: Did I draft language that creates a new legal commitment — the one thing kf-policy-ai-boundary says I may not do?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per draft: commitment-creating language detected?, the boundary text, verdict. Pair with whether the gate was ever exercised.

app_routes.name: Is the Chain Complete — /policy-drafting-agent/governance/approval-chain
app_routes.purpose: Before anything I rendered gets sent: has a human actually approved the MEANING, not just the formatting?
app_routes.layout_hints: Approval chain from draft to send, with each link's approver and scope. A formatting-only approval must not satisfy a meaning gate.

app_routes.name: Is My Draft Surviving Review — /policy-drafting-agent/quality/downstream-rewrite
app_routes.purpose: Is my draft surviving human review, or is noah-williams rewriting my legal language every time?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per draft: retained vs rewritten proportion, with the diff available. Aggregate rate in the header.

app_routes.name: May I Transmit — /notification-publisher/gates
app_routes.purpose: The four gates I evaluate before every send — channel permission, timing, content, and human authorization — as one verdict per intent.
app_routes.layout_hints: Gate matrix: intents down, four gates across, cell = pass/refuse. The row verdict is the conjunction. This is the agent's primary screen.

app_routes.name: Channel Permission — /notification-publisher/gates/channel-permission
app_routes.purpose: Am I permitted to use this channel for this recipient at all?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per intent: channel, recipient consent state, policy rule, verdict. The governing rule is named on every row.

app_routes.name: Timing Window — /notification-publisher/gates/timing
app_routes.purpose: Is the current moment inside a window this channel forbids?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per intent: send instant, recipient local time, forbidden window, verdict. This gate's refusals are temporary and must be labelled deferred, not blocked.

app_routes.name: Content Rules — /notification-publisher/gates/content
app_routes.purpose: Is the exact text I am holding within this channel's content rules?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per intent: length, segments, required opt-out, verdict. Show the computed values, never recompute them client-side.

app_routes.name: Human Authorization — /notification-publisher/gates/authorization
app_routes.purpose: Has every human authorization my instructions depend on actually been granted?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per intent: required authorizations, each granted or missing. A missing authorization is a hard refuse.

app_routes.name: Every Refusal — /notification-publisher/refusals
app_routes.purpose: When a gate refused, did the transmission actually stop — and did I invoke the documented exception instead?
app_routes.layout_hints: Refusal log: gate, verdict, did transmission stop, exception invoked. A refusal that did not stop the send is the most serious row on the screen.

app_routes.name: Every Refusal Leaves a Record — /notification-publisher/refusals/artifacts
app_routes.purpose: For every intent I refused, did I emit an artifact — a suppression record, an exception, anything a human could later find?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per refusal: artifact emitted?, its type and id. A refusal with no artifact is invisible to humans and is the finding.

app_routes.name: Deferred, Not Cancelled — /notification-publisher/refusals/deferred
app_routes.purpose: The timing gate is the only gate whose refusal is temporary — the window reopens. For every send I deferred, did it ever actually go?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per deferred intent: deferral instant, window reopen, eventual send or its absence. A deferral that never sent is a silent cancellation.

app_routes.name: After the Send — /notification-publisher/obligations
app_routes.purpose: policy-08 makes me responsible for collecting acknowledgements, not just for transmitting. Am I discharging that?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per delivery: acknowledgement expected?, received?, chased?. Transmission success is not obligation discharge and the layout must not imply it is.

app_routes.name: By What Authority Do I Hold This — /notification-publisher/self-check/my-authority
app_routes.route_name: By What Authority Do I Hold This
app_routes.purpose: I enforce authorization rules on every message I touch. By what recorded authority do I hold this role?
app_routes.layout_hints: My own assignment, its approver, and its validity — the same scrutiny I apply to others, applied to me.

app_routes.name: Am I the Only Witness — /notification-publisher/self-check/sole-witness
app_routes.purpose: Every gate I evaluate, I evaluate alone, and every result I record, I record about myself. Is there any claim about my behaviour that does not originate with me?
app_routes.layout_hints: Provenance of every claim about this agent, split by originator. If all originate with the agent, that is the finding and must be stated.

app_routes.name: Knowledge Health — /process-steward/health
app_routes.purpose: Where the register is thin: open gaps, overdue reviews, unstewarded versions, untested recovery paths.
app_routes.layout_hints: Four health tiles feeding four worklists. Every tile is a link, not a statistic.

app_routes.name: Cadence Breach — /process-steward/cadence/breach
app_routes.purpose: For close-v1.1.0 I promised a 90-day cadence and for policy-v1.0.0 a 60-day cadence. Is the ACTUAL interval inside what I promised?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per version: promised cadence, actual interval, delta. Computed against the modelled instant so the answer is reproducible.

app_routes.name: Was the Breach Remediated — /process-steward/cadence/remediation
app_routes.purpose: One review event exceeds the cadence I promised. Did anyone actually do anything about it?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per breach: the remediating action, or its absence. An unremediated breach is the finding; the breach alone is only the trigger.

app_routes.name: Live With a Blocking Gap — /process-steward/knowledge/open-gaps
app_routes.purpose: Is any procedure version live with an Open BLOCKING knowledge gap against it?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per version: open gaps by severity, blocking flag, owner. Live-and-blocking is the finding.

app_routes.name: Stalled Change Requests — /process-steward/governance/stalled-changes
app_routes.purpose: cr-policy-delivery was requested on 2026-07-19 with no DecidedAt. How long has it been sitting, and is that inside what we promised?
app_routes.layout_hints: Queue by age with the promised decision window marked. Overdue rows are the working list.

app_routes.name: Approved but Still Open — /process-steward/governance/approved-never-lands
app_routes.purpose: cr-close-timestamp is Approved, and the model still reads it as OPEN because IsOpen counts Approved as open. Every version it touches reads permanently unfit.
app_routes.layout_hints: Surface this as a MODEL DEFECT panel, not a data problem: the terminal-state gap, the rows it distorts, and the downstream verdicts it poisons.

app_routes.name: Versions With No Steward — /process-steward/ownership/orphan-versions
app_routes.purpose: Which procedure versions have no steward at all? close-v1.0.0 is Archived but still referenced.
app_routes.layout_hints: Per version: steward or none, status, inbound references. Unstewarded-but-referenced is the finding.

app_routes.name: Archived, Still Load-Bearing — /process-steward/ownership/archived-referenced
app_routes.purpose: close-v1.0.0 is Archived and unstewarded — but it is still referenced. What still points at it?
app_routes.layout_hints: Inbound reference list for each archived version. A referenced archive is not retired, and the page should say so.

app_routes.name: Untested Recovery Paths — /process-steward/knowledge/untested-fallbacks
app_routes.purpose: close-04-fallback-close-03 and policy-07-fallback-policy-06 are the paths we take when things go wrong. Have they ever been walked?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per fallback transition: times traversed, last traversal. Zero traversals is the finding.

app_routes.name: Which Untested Path Matters — /process-steward/knowledge/fallback-criticality
app_routes.purpose: Four recovery paths have never been walked. An untested path to a trivial step does not scare me; one guarding a blocking control does.
app_routes.layout_hints: Rank untested fallbacks by what they protect — blocking controls downstream, criticality of the target step. Ranking is the contribution here.

app_routes.name: Predicates Naming Step Ids — /process-steward/model/hardcoded-predicates
app_routes.purpose: Several of my predicates name individual steps by id. Steps.IsHumanApprovalGate hardcodes policy-05 and close-06 — it should key off a control kind instead.
app_routes.layout_hints: Model-quality worklist: predicates containing literal ids, with the generalisation each should use. This is technical debt in the rulebook, presented as such.

app_routes.name: Knowledge Register — /knowledge-authority/knowledge
app_routes.purpose: Every fragment: its status, its age, its owner, and whether anything live depends on it.
app_routes.layout_hints: Table with decay signals as columns rather than separate screens, so stacked fragility is visible in one pass.

app_routes.name: Compound Fragility — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/compound-fragility
app_routes.purpose: Four separate decay signals on knowledge fragments and no way to see where they stack. Show me where they compound.
app_routes.layout_hints: One row per fragment, one column per decay signal, plus a stack count. Sort by stack count — a fragment failing on four axes is categorically worse than four failing on one.

app_routes.name: Unapproved but Live — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/unapproved-live
app_routes.purpose: kf-policy-manager-route is Reviewed, not Approved, so IsCurrentlyValid is FALSE — and policy-08 is a live step depending on it.
app_routes.layout_hints: Per unapproved fragment: dependents, and whether each is live. Live dependents on an invalid fragment are the finding.

app_routes.name: Unapproved Knowledge Reaching Machines — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/reaching-machines
app_routes.purpose: One fragment is unapproved and operationally live, and all three AI boundaries are untested. Where does unapproved knowledge reach a machine that acts on it?
app_routes.layout_hints: Trace from unapproved fragments to software-executed steps. The intersection is the finding.

app_routes.name: Boundaries on Expired Claims — /knowledge-authority/governance/expired-ratifier
app_routes.purpose: RatifyingFragmentIsValid reads 2 of 3. One of the rules constraining what an AI agent may do is ratified by a fragment that is no longer valid.
app_routes.layout_hints: Per boundary: its ratifying fragment and that fragment's validity. An invalid ratifier undermines the boundary and must be shown as doing so.

app_routes.name: Orphaned Provenance — /knowledge-authority/governance/orphaned-provenance
app_routes.purpose: kf-close-fx-time, kf-close-top-ten and kf-close-judgment all trace to devon-okafor via elicit-close-shadow. If that provenance is orphaned, what rests on it?
app_routes.layout_hints: Provenance tree from agent through session to fragments, with the orphan state marked at whichever level it occurs.

app_routes.name: Semantic Change Without a Witness — /knowledge-authority/governance/unwitnessed-change
app_routes.purpose: cr-close-timestamp altered a blocking control and was decided by me. Did any semantic change go through without a witness?
app_routes.layout_hints: Per semantic change: what it altered, who decided, what witnessed the effect. A change with no witness is the finding.

app_routes.name: How Old Is the Evidence — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/elicitation-age
app_routes.purpose: elicit-close-shadow ran on 2026-04-03 and elicit-policy-workshop on 2026-05-10. How old is the evidence behind what we rely on?
app_routes.layout_hints: Sessions on a timeline with the fragments each produced, and the age of each. Judged against the modelled instant.

app_routes.name: Single-Witness Monoculture — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/method-monoculture
app_routes.purpose: 2 of 3 elicitation sessions used a single-witness method, and 4 of 7 fragments inherit that. How much of what we know rests on one person's account?
app_routes.layout_hints: Method distribution plus the inheritance chain into fragments. The inherited proportion is the headline.

app_routes.name: Known Unknowns — /knowledge-authority/knowledge/known-unknowns
app_routes.purpose: What do we know that we do not know? gap-policy-delivery-receipts has been Open since 2026-07-18 with a resolution nobody has taken.
app_routes.layout_hints: Gap register with age, owner, severity, and resolution path. Ownerless gaps sort first.

app_routes.name: Inferred, Not Recorded — /knowledge-authority/model/inferred-review-dates
app_routes.purpose: IsOverdueForReview reads 6/7 and I do not trust it — it is computed from AgeDays rather than from a recorded review date.
app_routes.layout_hints: Per fragment: inferred review state vs any recorded date. Where no date was ever recorded, say so — do not present the inference as a record.

app_routes.name: Step Execution — /shared/step-execution/:stepExecutionId
app_routes.purpose: One step execution, everything about it: spec, what happened, controls, evidence, issues.
app_routes.layout_hints: The existing step drawer promoted to a full route. Role-aware emphasis: the analyst sees controls first, the controller sees separation, the CFO sees approvals.

app_routes.name: Requirement — /shared/requirement/:requirementId
app_routes.purpose: One control: its statement, bindings, witness, and every evaluation.
app_routes.layout_hints: Header with statement and blocking flag; sections for bindings, witness scope, evaluation history.

app_routes.name: Knowledge Fragment — /shared/knowledge-fragment/:fragmentId
app_routes.purpose: One claim: its form, status, owner, provenance, and everything depending on it.
app_routes.layout_hints: Status and validity header; provenance chain up to the elicitation session; dependents fanned out below.

app_routes.name: Change Request — /shared/change-request/:changeRequestId
app_routes.purpose: One request: what it targets, who must clear it, and where it currently sits.
app_routes.layout_hints: Header with status and age; the authority chain; the version it targets.

app_routes.name: Exception — /shared/exception/:exceptionId
app_routes.purpose: One documented exception: its condition, its handling, and every time it was invoked.
app_routes.layout_hints: Condition and handling text, approval and fallback roles, invocation history.

app_routes.name: Role Assignment — /shared/role-assignment/:assignmentId
app_routes.purpose: One assignment: who held what, when, on whose authority.
app_routes.layout_hints: Validity window rendered as a timeline; approver and predecessor named.

app_routes.name: Operational Binding — /shared/operational-binding/:bindingId
app_routes.purpose: One binding: its source, freshness SLA, authoritative flag, and observation history.
app_routes.layout_hints: Freshness judged against the modelled instant, with the instant named on the page.

app_routes.name: Delivery — /shared/delivery/:deliveryId
app_routes.purpose: One delivery: intended, sent, landed, acknowledged — plus the exact text transmitted.
app_routes.layout_hints: Lifecycle strip across the top; frozen text below; gate results attached.

app_routes.name: Recipient — /shared/recipient/:recipientId
app_routes.purpose: One person: consent state, channels, every message we attempted, and whether we ever reached them.
app_routes.layout_hints: Consent history as a timeline; attempts listed with outcomes.

app_routes.name: Message Template — /shared/template/:templateId
app_routes.purpose: One template: its text, approvals, edit history, and every send that used it.
app_routes.layout_hints: Edit history against approval history on one axis — that overlay is what makes drift visible.

app_routes.name: Procedure Version — /shared/procedure-version/:versionId
app_routes.purpose: One version: its steps, status, stewardship, reviews, and what still references it.
app_routes.layout_hints: Header with status and steward; steps listed; inbound references shown even when archived.

app_routes.name: Knowledge Gap — /shared/knowledge-gap/:gapId
app_routes.purpose: One gap: what is missing, who owns closing it, how long it has been open, and what it blocks.
app_routes.layout_hints: Age and severity in the header; blocked items listed below.

app_routes.name: Verification Outcome — /shared/verification-outcome/:outcomeId
app_routes.purpose: One verification: expected signal, observed signal, observer, and independence.
app_routes.layout_hints: Expected vs observed side by side; independence verdict prominent.

app_routes.name: Review Event — /shared/review-event/:reviewId
app_routes.purpose: One review: kind, reviewer, outcome, and when the next is due.
app_routes.layout_hints: Cadence context in the header so a single review reads against its promised interval.

app_routes.name: Elicitation Session — /shared/elicitation-session/:sessionId
app_routes.purpose: One session: method, participants, date, and every fragment it produced.
app_routes.layout_hints: Method and single-witness flag in the header; produced fragments listed with their current validity.

app_routes.name: Step Transition — /shared/transition/:transitionId
app_routes.purpose: One transition: from, to, condition, kind, and how often it has actually been taken.
app_routes.layout_hints: Traversal count prominent — a zero on a fallback is the point of the page.

app_routes.name: Authority Boundary — /shared/authority-boundary/:boundaryId
app_routes.purpose: One boundary: what it constrains, the fragment ratifying it, and whether it has ever been tested.
app_routes.layout_hints: Ratifier validity and 'ever approached' count together — neither alone answers the question.

app_routes.name: Evaluation Context — /shared/evaluation-context
app_routes.purpose: The modelled instant every time-dependent answer in this app is judged against.
app_routes.layout_hints: State the instant plainly, list the columns that depend on it, and explain why the wall clock is not used.

app_routes.name: Field Provenance — /shared/field/:table/:field
app_routes.purpose: Any field, traced back to the question that motivated it and the formula that computes it.
app_routes.layout_hints: The existing provenance tracer promoted to a route so every value in the app is deep-linkable.

app_routes.name: Choose a Role — /
app_routes.purpose: The entry point: one card per role, each carrying its own colour and icon.
app_routes.layout_hints: Grid of 12 role cards, human roles first then software roles, each with icon, label, responsibility, and question count. Selecting a card enters that role's dashboard.

app_routes.name: Test Board — /admin/conformance
app_routes.purpose: Every check the model runs against itself, and whether the board is green.
app_routes.layout_hints: Green/red banner with a blocking-failure count, then per-suite and per-kind tables, then the filterable check list. Warnings are advisory and must read that way — scoring a non-firing witness red would only pressure someone into fabricating rows until it went green.

app_routes.name: Checks — /admin/conformance/checks
app_routes.purpose: One row per check, filterable by kind, outcome, and subject.
app_routes.layout_hints: Filter bar over a virtualised list. Each row shows outcome, subject, assertion, and the question it defends. Blocking and advisory are visually distinct.

app_routes.name: Witness Board — /admin/witnesses
app_routes.purpose: Every boolean witness with its live true/false distribution, so a column that cannot discriminate is visible rather than mistaken for a working check.
app_routes.layout_hints: Grouped by table. Per witness: fire count, distribution bar, and a verdict of discriminates / always-true / never-true / empty. Non-vacuity is the acceptance bar, so the vacuous ones are reported, never hidden.

app_routes.name: Cannot Discriminate — /admin/witnesses/vacuous
app_routes.purpose: The witnesses that read the same value on every row — they state nothing about the procedures and are not evidence.
app_routes.layout_hints: Working list of vacuous witnesses with, for each, whether uniformity is legitimate (every seeded requirement really is blocking) or a defect. Do not present these as failures; present them as unproven.

app_routes.name: Loops & Questions — /admin/loops
app_routes.purpose: The expansion loops: what each made askable, which role asked, and how many predicates each question produced.
app_routes.layout_hints: Loop sections, each with its premise, then questions grouped by asking role. Each question shows its predicate count and computed answer.

app_routes.name: Question Defence — /admin/loops/question/:questionId
app_routes.purpose: One question: the predicates invented to answer it, the checks defending it, and the routes where a role actually asks it.
app_routes.layout_hints: Three panels — predicates, checks, routes. The routes panel reads AppRouteQuestions, closing the loop between the question and the screens built to answer it.

app_routes.name: Provenance Tracer — /admin/provenance
app_routes.purpose: Trace any field back to the question that motivated it, the role that asked, and the loop it came from.
app_routes.layout_hints: Search by Table.Field, then a chain: field → question → role → loop, plus sibling predicates from the same question. Fields predating the loops carry no question and must say so — inventing one retroactively would be fabrication.

app_routes.name: Route Map — /admin/route-map
app_routes.purpose: The application's own navigation model: every route, which questions it answers, and which routes it links to.
app_routes.layout_hints: Matrix or graph of AppRoutes against AppRouteQuestions, with an explicit panel for AnswersNoQuestion — a route serving no question should be justified or removed.

app_routes.name: Catalog Drift — /admin/model/catalog-drift
app_routes.purpose: Whether the field catalog still matches the real schemas, and whether every catalog field resolves to a column the substrate actually emitted.
app_routes.layout_hints: Two checks side by side: catalog-vs-schema drift, and catalog-vs-information_schema resolution. Both must state 'in sync' explicitly rather than rendering an empty list.

app_routes.name: Every Inference — /explorer/inferences
app_routes.purpose: All 937 derived fields with the formula that defines it and the fields it reads.
app_routes.layout_hints: Stat row (raw vs inferred, and by kind), then a filterable list. Each entry shows its formula with field references highlighted, its dependencies, and the question that motivated it.

app_routes.name: All Tables — /explorer/tables
app_routes.purpose: Every table with its raw/calculated/lookup/aggregation composition.
app_routes.layout_hints: Table index with a composition bar per row. Infrastructure tables that deliberately have no view are labelled as such, not as broken.

app_routes.name: Table Detail — /explorer/tables/:table
app_routes.purpose: One table: its full column catalog and every row, with inferred columns distinguished from stated ones.
app_routes.layout_hints: Column cards above a row grid. Inferred columns are shaded and their cells are clickable for the formula-and-inputs popover.

app_routes.name: Record Inspector — /explorer/record/:table/:id
app_routes.purpose: One row, every field it has: stated values first, then each inference with the current value of every field its formula reads.
app_routes.layout_hints: Two sections — stated and inferred. Each inference shows its formula and its inputs, local or across a foreign key, with derived inputs marked so the chain can be walked further back.

knowledge_gaps.name: High: No validated fallback exists for simultaneous ERP and signed
knowledge_gaps.statement: No validated fallback exists for simultaneous ERP and signed-snapshot repository outage.
knowledge_gaps.resolution_plan: Resolved by adding offline signed export escrow.

knowledge_gaps.name: Medium: SMS provider delivery receipts are not always final for port
knowledge_gaps.statement: SMS provider delivery receipts are not always final for ported numbers.

knowledge_gaps.name: High: req-close-separation stated the preparer may not be the fina
knowledge_gaps.statement: req-close-separation stated the preparer may not be the final approver, but nothing evaluated it. The control existed only as prose in a Requirements row, so a violation would have been invisible.
knowledge_gaps.resolution_plan: Resolved by StepExecutions.ViolatesSeparationOfDuties, which counts preparation steps in the same procedure execution performed by the agent now approving. Verified by staging a breach (maria-chen approving se-close05 after preparing se-close03): the witness read TRUE. The staged breach was reverted; the control now reads FALSE because separation genuinely holds, not because nothing is checking.

knowledge_gaps.name: Medium: StewardshipAssignments promised a 90-day review cadence for
knowledge_gaps.statement: StewardshipAssignments promised a 90-day review cadence for close-v1.1.0 and 60 days for policy-v1.0.0. Both the promise and the actual review history were in the model and nothing compared them, so a lapsed cadence was invisible.
knowledge_gaps.resolution_plan: Resolved by ReviewEvents.ExceedsPromisedCadence and PromiseAndBehaviorDisagree, which compare DaysSinceReviewed against the cadence promised by the version's stewardship assignment. Surfacing the real Q1 review (review-close-q1) showed the witness firing on genuine history: 121 days elapsed against a 90-day promise. The Q2 review closed the lapse, so current state reads compliant.

knowledge_gaps.name: High: Five of twelve roles were held only by a denormalized Roles.
knowledge_gaps.statement: Five of twelve roles were held only by a denormalized Roles.CurrentAgent pointer with no RoleAssignments row: communications-manager, knowledge-authority, process-steward, close-automation, policy-drafting-agent. The convenience pointer claimed a holder the auditable time-bounded table could not confirm, so provenance for anything those roles touched was unverifiable.
knowledge_gaps.resolution_plan: Surfaced by Agents.IsStillEngaged, which counts CURRENT RoleAssignments rather than trusting Roles.CurrentAgent. amina-yusuf read as not engaged, which made kf-policy-channel an IsUndefendableTacitClaim. Resolved by recording the five missing time-bounded assignments. The witness stays: it is the only thing that distinguishes a real appointment from a denormalized pointer.

knowledge_gaps.name: Critical: comm-sms-policy set ConsentRequired=true and exc-no-sms-cons
knowledge_gaps.statement: comm-sms-policy set ConsentRequired=true and exc-no-sms-consent documented the suppress-and-email handling, but no per-recipient delivery record existed, so a send to a non-consenting recipient was structurally invisible. req-policy-consent was a blocking control with zero satisfaction records.
knowledge_gaps.resolution_plan: Resolved by the Recipients and MessageDeliveries tables plus MessageDeliveries.IsConsentViolation. Proven on md-003, a real SMS to a never-consented recipient, which the witness flags while correctly NOT flagging md-004 (consent revoked, properly suppressed under exc-no-sms-consent) or md-006 (unreachable, failed, HR case opened). Recipient re-consented; the delivery row is retained as evidence.

knowledge_gaps.name: High: comm-sms-policy defined a 20:00-08:00 quiet window and nothi
knowledge_gaps.statement: comm-sms-policy defined a 20:00-08:00 quiet window and nothing compared a send time against it.
knowledge_gaps.resolution_plan: Resolved by MessageDeliveries.IsInsideQuietWindow and IsQuietHoursViolation, proven on md-005 (21:00 send). QuietHoursStartHour is stored rather than parsed: VALUE(LEFT("20:00",2)) does not translate — the transpiler casts the string to a timestamp and the view errors.

knowledge_gaps.name: Critical: MessageTemplates carried Status="Approved" as a bare string
knowledge_gaps.statement: MessageTemplates carried Status="Approved" as a bare string with no approval record behind it, and nothing evaluated a send BEFORE transmission. Every gate the communication policies define — consent, quiet hours, length, opt-out, approval — was checkable only after the fact, if at all.
knowledge_gaps.resolution_plan: Resolved by the SendIntents table and IsClearedToSend, which gates a proposed send on permission, timing, content, and authorization before it happens, and names the blocking gate. Proven across seven intents: Timing blocks a 21:00 send, Content blocks an oversized body and one missing the STOP phrase, Permission blocks an unreachable recipient. Authorization blocked ALL sends until tmpl-policy-sms received a real approval record (tap-sms-001) — the pipeline had been transmitting under a template nobody had attributably approved.

role_assignments.name: knowledge-authority @ 2026-01-01 00:00:00-06
role_assignments.reason: Knowledge authority vested with the CFO for financial procedures

role_questions.name: finance-analyst: On the steps I personally executed, did any of them close ou
role_questions.question_text: On the steps I personally executed, did any of them close out while a BLOCKING requirement was still not fully satisfied?
role_questions.why_it_matters: I executed se-close03 (Reconcile material accounts), which carries TWO blocking requirements via sr-c03a (req-close-balance) and sr-c03b (req-close-evidence). Today the model records SatisfactionLevel as free text and nothing compares it against IsBlocking. If I close a step with a PartiallySatisfied blocking control — exactly the shape sat-policy-legal is in right now — the package moves on and nobody is told. I want that to be a computed red flag on my own row before it becomes an audit finding on my name.

role_questions.name: finance-analyst: Which blocking requirements were attached to a step I ran bu
role_questions.question_text: Which blocking requirements were attached to a step I ran but never got a satisfaction record at all — not satisfied, not unsatisfied, just never assessed?
role_questions.why_it_matters: This is the failure mode that scares me more than a recorded 'Unsatisfied'. sr-c03b binds req-close-evidence to close-03. I ran close-03 as se-close03. There is no RequirementSatisfactions row for that pairing. The model shows green because absence reads as silence, not as a gap. An unevaluated blocking control is indistinguishable from a passed one, and that is the exact thing SOX testing is designed to catch.

role_questions.name: finance-analyst: When I attested my reconciliation, was the underlying ledger
role_questions.question_text: When I attested my reconciliation, was the underlying ledger data actually fresh — or was I certifying against a source that had already gone stale under its own SLA?
role_questions.why_it_matters: OperationalBindings.IsFresh already exists and works, but it is evaluated against NOW() and lives on a table nothing in the execution story reads. My step execution has no idea whether the resources it depended on were inside their freshness SLA. se-close02 already recorded a 17-minute feed against a 15-minute SLA and it took a human writing prose into a Deviation field to surface it. I want that connected structurally, because next time the prose might not get written.

role_questions.name: finance-analyst: Which of my steps ran long without anybody recording why — a
role_questions.question_text: Which of my steps ran long without anybody recording why — and of those, which ones had an exception available that nobody invoked?
role_questions.why_it_matters: StepExecutions.IsLate already works. But 'late' on its own is not a finding; late-and-unexplained is. se-close03 is mine and it ran nearly 19 hours. If that overran the expected duration and the Deviation field is empty, I have an undocumented overrun sitting on my name. And exc-ledger-outage exists precisely for the close-02 condition — if it was never invoked, the model should say that out loud instead of letting a blank Deviation stand in for 'nothing happened'.

role_questions.name: finance-analyst: For every step I ran that had a declared verification, did a
role_questions.question_text: For every step I ran that had a declared verification, did anybody actually perform it and record the observed signal — or did I just get a PASS with nothing behind it?
role_questions.why_it_matters: StepVerifications is entirely spec-side. verify-reconciliation declares that close-03 must show unexplained-material-variance = 0. I ran close-03. My StepExecution says VerificationResult=PASS. But there is no row anywhere recording what the signal ACTUALLY read. The PASS is an unbacked assertion typed into a field. If an auditor asks me to produce the observed value, the model has nothing — and a skipped verification looks identical to a passed one.

role_questions.name: controller: Did the same agent both prepare and approve any part of this
role_questions.question_text: Did the same agent both prepare and approve any part of this close? req-close-separation says the preparer may not be the final approver — show me that it actually held, on exec-close-2026-q2, computed and not asserted.
role_questions.why_it_matters: This is the single highest-value gap in the model and it is my control. req-close-separation is IsBlocking=true, bound to close-05 via sr-c05, and sat-close-separation records SatisfactionLevel='Satisfied' with the evidence string 'Preparer and reviewer were different agents.' That string is a human typing a conclusion into a text field. NOTHING compares se-close03.ExecutedByAgent (maria-chen) against se-close05.ExecutedByAgent (devon-okafor) or se-close06.ExecutedByAgent (priya-raman). Segregation of duties is the control SOX cares about most and in this model it is prose. If maria-chen executed both the preparation and the approval tomorrow, sat-close-separation would still say 'Satisfied' and the model would agree.

role_questions.name: controller: Every approval on this close — was it given by an agent who
role_questions.question_text: Every approval on this close — was it given by an agent who actually held the required role AT THE TIME they approved, not just someone who holds it today?
role_questions.why_it_matters: req-close-human-approval is blocking and says controller and CFO approvals must be human-confirmed. sat-close-human records 'Satisfied' because a human name appears in a field. But nothing checks that the approving agent held the approving role. RoleAssignments proves this is not paranoia: ra-old-variance shows maria-chen held variance-review-agent until 2026-03-31 and ra-new-variance shows variance-ai took it on 2026-04-01. Role-holding is time-bounded and it genuinely changes. If someone approves close-06 who is not the CFO, or who was the CFO last quarter but not this one, I need that computed. And exc-cfo-unavailable explicitly permits delegation to an Acting CFO 'never to the preparer' — so an authority check that cannot see delegation is incomplete.

role_questions.name: controller: Which of my blocking close controls are structurally incapab
role_questions.question_text: Which of my blocking close controls are structurally incapable of failing — declared, bound to a step, and yet with no mechanism that could ever produce a negative result?
role_questions.why_it_matters: req-close-cutoff, req-close-balance, req-close-separation, and req-close-evidence are all IsBlocking=true. All four are pure prose. A control that cannot fail is not a control, it is a comment. Before I sign anything I want a list of my own controls ranked by whether they can actually operate. This is the meta-question — it is about the model's ability to hold me accountable, and it is the one I would ask first if I were the external auditor rather than the controller.

role_questions.name: controller: Give me one number per close: did exec-close-2026-q2 actuall
role_questions.question_text: Give me one number per close: did exec-close-2026-q2 actually conform to close-v1.1.0, and if not, how far off was it?
role_questions.why_it_matters: ProcedureExecutions has ZERO derived fields. The parent of the entire execution story makes no claim whatsoever — it has a status someone typed and two timestamps. Every failure signal in this model lives on child rows, so to know whether a close was clean I have to read twelve StepExecutions and six RequirementSatisfactions by hand. That is not a control environment, that is a filing cabinet. I want conformance to be a computed property of the execution, so that 'the close was clean' is a claim the model makes and can be wrong about.

role_questions.name: controller: Did any AI agent or automated pipeline execute a step that r
role_questions.question_text: Did any AI agent or automated pipeline execute a step that requires human confirmation, or sign off on something a human was supposed to own?
role_questions.why_it_matters: req-close-human-approval and req-policy-human-approval both say a human must approve. Steps carries RequiresHumanConfirmation as a raw boolean and Agents carries AgentKind — Human, AIAgent, AutomatedPipeline — and NOTHING compares them. variance-ai executed se-close04. policy-drafting-ai executed se-policy03. Both fine today because those steps are not approval steps. But ra-old-variance to ra-new-variance shows this org actively migrates work from humans to AI agents, and the control that is supposed to stop that migration reaching an approval step is prose. This is the control I expect to matter most over the next two years and it currently does not exist.

role_questions.name: cfo: Can I sign the attestation for exec-close-2026-q2 — yes or n
role_questions.question_text: Can I sign the attestation for exec-close-2026-q2 — yes or no — and if no, name the blocker.
role_questions.why_it_matters: This is the only question I actually have. Today the model answers it with ProcedureExecutions.ExecutionStatus='Completed', which is a string somebody typed into a field. My signature carries personal liability under Section 302. I need attestation-readiness to be a computed conjunction of every blocking control, such that if ANY control did not operate, the model says no and names it. A green status that cannot go red is worse than no status at all, because it manufactures false comfort at exactly the moment I am least able to verify it myself.

role_questions.name: cfo: Am I being asked to approve an execution of a procedure vers
role_questions.question_text: Am I being asked to approve an execution of a procedure version that is itself overdue for review, or that has an open change request against it?
role_questions.why_it_matters: I sign against close-v1.1.0. If that version's periodic review lapsed, or if there is an open ChangeRequest saying the procedure is known to be wrong, then I am attesting to conformance with a specification that the organization itself no longer stands behind. ReviewEvents.IsOverdue already works and ChangeRequests.IsOpen already works, but neither is connected to the execution I am signing. The version's fitness and the execution's conformance are two different questions and I need both answered before I sign, not one.

role_questions.name: cfo: My own approval on se-close06 — is there anything behind it
role_questions.question_text: My own approval on se-close06 — is there anything behind it other than the fact that I clicked approve?
role_questions.why_it_matters: verify-cfo declares that close-06 must show cfo-approval = APPROVED. se-close06 says VerificationResult=PASS. But the PASS and the approval are the same act: I approved, therefore the verification that I approved passes. That is circular, and it is my name on the circle. sat-close-human's evidence reads 'Human CFO approval recorded' — recorded by whom, against what? I want to know whether my approval rests on independently verified upstream evidence or whether the model is simply reflecting my own click back at me.

role_questions.name: cfo: For every approval in this close, tell me the human who was
role_questions.question_text: For every approval in this close, tell me the human who was personally accountable — and whether an exception was used to route authority away from the person who normally holds it.
role_questions.why_it_matters: exc-cfo-unavailable exists and says approval may be delegated to a designated Acting CFO, 'never to the preparer'. That last clause is a control and it is prose inside a text field. If I was unavailable and someone approved in my place, I need the model to show me who, under what authority, and whether the never-to-the-preparer condition held. Right now an exception can be invoked with no trace at all — nothing links an execution back to the exception it used. From my seat that means delegated authority is entirely invisible, which is the exposure I am least willing to carry.

role_questions.name: cfo: Across everything I am signing, is there any control claim i
role_questions.question_text: Across everything I am signing, is there any control claim in this model that rests on a human typing a conclusion rather than on something computed?
role_questions.why_it_matters: This is the question behind all my other questions. sat-close-separation says 'Preparer and reviewer were different agents.' sat-close-human says 'Human CFO approval recorded.' Both are prose conclusions in an Evidence field, both assert that a control operated, and neither is checkable. I want the model to distinguish between a control that was COMPUTED to have held and one that was ASSERTED to have held, and to tell me how much of my attestation rests on the second kind. If most of my assurance is assertion, I want to know that before I sign, not after.

role_questions.name: process-steward: For close-v1.1.0 I promised a 90-day review cadence and for
role_questions.question_text: For close-v1.1.0 I promised a 90-day review cadence and for policy-v1.0.0 a 60-day cadence. Is the ACTUAL interval since the last review already longer than the cadence I promised?
role_questions.why_it_matters: ReviewCadenceDays is a promise. ReviewEvents.ReviewedAt is the behavior. Today the model stores both and compares neither, so a stewardship assignment can sit in permanent silent breach while ReviewEvents.IsOverdue stays FALSE because NextReviewDue was hand-set to a date that has nothing to do with the promised cadence. I need the promise and the behavior in the same row.

role_questions.name: process-steward: Which procedure versions have no steward at all? close-v1.0.
role_questions.question_text: Which procedure versions have no steward at all? close-v1.0.0 is Archived but still referenced by ProcedureVersionLinks — does anyone own it?
role_questions.why_it_matters: An unstewarded version is nobody's problem until it is everybody's problem. There are 3 ProcedureVersions and only 2 StewardshipAssignments; the model has never once been asked to notice the difference. Orphaned versions accumulate silently as new versions ship and the old assignment is never extended or retired.

role_questions.name: process-steward: close-04-fallback-close-03 and policy-07-fallback-policy-06
role_questions.question_text: close-04-fallback-close-03 and policy-07-fallback-policy-06 are the paths we take when things go wrong. Have they EVER been walked in a real execution?
role_questions.why_it_matters: There are 19 StepTransitions and only 12 StepExecutions. Every Fallback and Alternative transition in this model is untested. Untested fallbacks are exactly where an outage becomes an incident — the day the ERP is down is the wrong day to discover the recovery path was never real. Nothing in the model witnesses this.
role_questions.witnessed_answer: StepExecutions.IsCompleted=12/12; StepTransitions.HasBeenTraversed=10/19; StepTransitions.HasReachableOrigin=14/19; StepTransitions.HasReachableTarget=13/19; StepTransitions.IsNeverExercised=6/19; StepTransitions.IsRecoveryPath=4/19; StepTransitions.IsUntestedRecoveryPath=1/19; StepTransitions.IsUnwalkedRecoveryPath=4/19

role_questions.name: process-steward: Is any procedure version live with an Open BLOCKING knowledg
role_questions.question_text: Is any procedure version live with an Open BLOCKING knowledge gap against it?
role_questions.why_it_matters: gap-close-dual-outage was Blocking and is now Resolved — good. But nothing stops the next one from staying Open while the version keeps shipping. ProcedureVersions.CountOfOpenKnowledgeGaps exists but is blind to BlockingKind, so a Blocking gap and a cosmetic one count the same. IsReadyForExecution then fails on trivia and stays silent on the thing that should stop the line.

role_questions.name: process-steward: cr-policy-delivery was requested on 2026-07-19 and has no De
